Uzbek-> Bukhara -> Mughals

I play very aggressively, so I am always trying to find the next war and be ready to swoop in when a neighbor is weak. So this game I set the personal goal of all of Asia.

First time going for this run, doing alright. Uzbek start in a good position to eat like four close by nations and become the super Steppe Horde. Had several hiccups in it though. The change from Uzbek to Bukhara was one of them, I could not afford enough of an army to hold all my lands. It took time to develop back to my proper aggressive position. The change from Bukhara to Mughal was another, because the army is worse than their older kind, going Indian is tough.

1688 and I have most of Asia under thumb if not outright a part of my nation, Europe has had a few pushes in but I have funded rebellions to get rid of them.

My goal is going to be hit, I want all of Asia under my control, it will be tough to get those colonialized islands though, those are almost all European already.

I've never really gotten into hordes much, mostly been playing as baby western nations (I'm a big fan of the Iberian peninsula nations, mostly because I really like colonizing for some unfathomable reason) the small nations on the Arabian peninsula, and the Japanese Daimyos.

I've been thinking once I get bored of my current Spain game I'll do a Horde (maybe Haixi?)> Manchu > Qing game or finally get the Inca sun god achievement.

Horde play can be tough, it has highs and lows in it that make for something of a rollercoaster. Any one of the other Hordes could make a play on you at any time if you're not allies, no need for claims at all.

You can support a good sized army and basically steal any land you want without having to deal with a coalition forming as long as you expand in a circle. By circle I mean that you expand north, east, south, west, and then back to north. It helps prevent people from getting too pissed at you.

Switching to Bukhara is nice after you have destroyed all the other hordes and have surrounded and separated all the near by nations for later consumption, but it takes a lot out of your economy to do so. The step from Steppe to a landed nation means you almost halve your military. Not sure how that would play into Haixi, but that is something to be careful of.

It's nice to go back to an old fave. It's not nice releveling everything, but that was half the fun the first go round. My official account can still be reactivated and I try to do so every other year to keep it alive, but so much has changed. The private server has it locked at around the 2007 expansions and updates which suits me perfectly since it's where the game last was when I stopped playing seriously.

Was sad to hear that the end of this game is cominh soon. Is the private server anygood? Maybe the pros and cons? I would love to start this back up and get into, its something I have been regretting not doing for a while now.

I don't think the PC version is going anywhere anytime soon. Console version is being shut down later this year.

I only know the private server I'm on. There are others but can't speak for them. The guy who runs and started the one I'm on basically laid it out as a retirement home for FFXI players.

Content is rolled back to 2007 as best as possible. It's not perfect some stuff just isn't coded or not entirely understood, but most of its all there pre Wings of the Goddess and the first 3 missions of ToAU.

So far everyone is pretty nice and chill. Heavy GM presence that have all been super helpful and friendly.

Upwards of 100 or so people on at max times usually about 40 to 60 on at all times. With level sync there's always groups xping but with a server set 200% xp bonus and the books from Wings of the Goddess in the pre wings zones soloing to 75 is entirely possible on most classes.

The private server is somewhat dependant on an updated retail copy but retail just got its final update so getting up and running is pretty easy. You do need to own a licensed copy of the game as you have to boot up play online and do an update via file check.

All in all I love it. There's daily Dynamis where the currency is duped to all players so there's a load of people running around with their completed relic weapons. Then there's people like me who's taking every class to 75. So far about 10 out of 18 to 50 and most of the rest are to 32.

All crafts can be taken to 100 and there is a location set up to do just that and almost everything on the AH is 2g and periodically restocked with some exceptions like Leaping Boots and K Clubs gotta work for those and the drops rates are only slightly better than retail.
